payload.big_idea: The iteration process itself is a drawn state machine: the same Advanced Canvas the owner sketches in Obsidian compiles into the executor that drives agent sessions through day-scale iterations - parallel branches run in parallel, owner gates block mechanically, and the working laws (1s interactive, milestone-scoped verification, gate-bound commits) are engine refusals, not prose. Lineage: v1's quack engine (deterministic gates, walk laws baked as refusals in i22) + v2's machines-are-canvases (i2f) and the drawn systematic machine (i2g).
payload.to_be_world: The owner redlines a machine drawing in Obsidian over morning coffee; the change IS the process change - no code, no prompt edits. A session boots, names its project, and the machine hands it packets; on parallel branches two agents hold two states of the same iteration at once, and the board shows both tokens side by side. Long work runs in the background - no call holds the owner's board hostage for 5 seconds. When a gate ripens, the offer surfaces on the board (later the phone); one bless advances the machine, and the commit lands right after, never in between. The next morning, opening an iteration starts with the retro: the inbox drains, one generic log query surfaces where the process rubbed, and the kickoff handover carries the whole plan in one brief.
payload.goal_system: G1 executor: the drawn systematic machine runs (tokens, joins, parallel activation, sub-machine seeding). G2 owner control: gates, board visibility, one-brief handovers. G3 working rhythm: 1s rule, updates on submit, gate-bound commits. G4 self-improvement: retro flow with generic log aggregation. Conflicts, named openly: (a) mechanical enforcement vs agent flexibility - ruled for enforcement, the machine catches errors, the agent stops pre-checking; (b) parallel speed vs serialized owner attention - the offer queue serializes adjudication while work parallelizes; (c) one day-scale iteration vs 20 steps of engine law - the honest risk of i3; priority order ruled by the plan: executor and retro flow first, engine laws ride behind them.
payload.moore_pitch: FOR a solo engineer driving AI agents on serious projects, WHO needs day-scale iterations to stay controlled without babysitting the agent, quackitect v2's SE machine IS a process engine THAT compiles hand-drawn state machines into mechanically enforced agent workflows; UNLIKE prompt-discipline harnesses that ask the model to behave, the engine refuses illegal moves at the tool boundary - the drawing is the law.
